message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No Speed Limit” signs are common on rural highways; drivers must drive at a safe speed. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – *Speed Limits* page | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or under 4 ft 9 in must be in a child safety seat. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | TxDOT – *Distracted Driving* | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – *DUI* | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles turning left must yield to oncoming traffic. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School‑Bus Rules** | • Stop when a school bus stops and displays red lights.
• Do not pass a stopped school bus until it resumes motion. | TxDOT – *School Bus Safety* | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not pass on the right unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a stop sign, crosswalk, or intersection.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited. | TxDOT – *Parking* | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Vehicles must display valid registration stickers.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) – *Vehicle Inspection* | | **Emergency Vehicle Rules** | • Drivers must pull over to the right and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **High‑way Use & Toll Roads** | • Texas has both toll and free interstate segments.
• Toll roads require electronic payment (e‑Tag). | TxDOT – *Toll Roads* | | **Penalties for Traffic Violations** | • Points added to driver’s record; 4 points can lead to license suspension.
• Fines vary by violation type. | Texas DMV – *Traffic Ticket Information* | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official website provides current statutes, posted speed limits, and safety campaigns. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text governing all traffic rules. 3. **Texas DMV** – Handles registration, licensing, and penalty information. 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific case law or recent rulings affecting traffic regulations. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re designed for local conditions. - **Keep a safe following distance** – especially on highways where speeds are higher. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk or navigate. - **Check for school‑bus signals** before passing any stopped bus. - **Stay alert for construction zones** – speed limits often drop significantly. Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper details on any specific area (e.g., DUI penalties, school‑bus rules, or how to handle a traffic ticket).
